title: A connected base-changed image gives an invariant nontrivial separation
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $L/k$ be a finite Galois extension [def-pc-field-extension]: $L$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal (the minimal polynomial over $k$ of every element of $L$ splits in $L$). Let $f:T\to X$ be a morphism of schemes over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], write $f_L:T_L\to X_L$ for its base change [def-pc-base-change], and assume $T_L$ is connected, including nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}(L/k)$ and, for $\sigma\in G$, put $\sigma_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $X_L=A\amalg B$ is a partition into two nonempty open and closed subsets. After possibly interchanging $A$ and $B$, the subsets
$$
P=\bigcap_{\sigma\in G}\sigma_X(A),\qquad Q=X_L\setminus P
$$
are nonempty, open and closed, satisfy $X_L=P\amalg Q$ and $f_L(T_L)\subseteq P\subseteq A$, and obey $\sigma_X(P)=P$ and $\sigma_X(Q)=Q$ for every $\sigma\in G$. No connectedness assumption on $X$ or geometric connectedness assumption on $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, first paragraph and the displayed intersection/union construction, specialized to finite Galois L/k; action in equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar.

proof.text: Let $I=f_L(T_L)$. The inverse images $f_L^{-1}(A)$ and $f_L^{-1}(B)$ are complementary open and closed subsets of $T_L$: inverse images under the continuous underlying map of a scheme morphism preserve opens, closed sets, complements, and unions [def-pc-scheme]. By the definition of connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme], one inverse image is empty. Interchange $A,B$ if necessary so that $f_L^{-1}(B)=\varnothing$. Then $I\subseteq A$, and $I\ne\varnothing$ since $T_L\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, first paragraph and finite-Galois intersection/union construction; equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar for the opposite action.

proof.text: For $Y=T,X$, functoriality of the spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-base-change] give $1_Y=\mathrm{id}_{Y_L}$ and $(\sigma\circ\tau)_Y=\tau_Y\circ\sigma_Y$: both sides have the same two projections. In particular $(\sigma^{-1})_Y$ is inverse to $\sigma_Y$, so these are homeomorphisms, their underlying maps and inverses being continuous scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme]. The same projection check gives $f_L\circ\sigma_T=\sigma_X\circ f_L$: the projections to $X$ are both $f\circ\mathrm{pr}_T$, and the projections to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ are both $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ\mathrm{pr}_L$. Thus $\sigma_X(I)=f_L(\sigma_T(T_L))=I$.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, first paragraph and finite-Galois intersection/union construction; equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar for the opposite action.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] with $M=L$: the assumed finite-dimensionality, separability and normality are exactly its hypotheses, so $G$ is finite. Every $\sigma_X(A)$ is open and closed, because it is the inverse image of $A$ under the continuous inverse homeomorphism $(\sigma^{-1})_X$. Hence $P=\bigcap_{\sigma\in G}\sigma_X(A)$ is open and closed: a finite intersection of opens is open, and its complement is a finite union of open complements. Therefore $Q=X_L\setminus P$ is also open and closed.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, first paragraph and finite-Galois intersection/union construction; equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar for the opposite action.

proof.text: For every $\sigma\in G$, step 2 and $I\subseteq A$ give $I=\sigma_X(I)\subseteq\sigma_X(A)$; thus $I\subseteq P$, so $P$ is nonempty. The identity automorphism occurs among the indices, so $P\subseteq1_X(A)=A$. Consequently $B\subseteq X_L\setminus P=Q$, so $Q$ is nonempty. The definition of $Q$ gives $X_L=P\amalg Q$.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, first paragraph and finite-Galois intersection/union construction; equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar for the opposite action.

proof.text: Fix $\tau\in G$. A bijection carries an intersection to the intersection of its images: a point belongs on either side precisely when its unique inverse image belongs to every member of the family. Using the opposite composition law from step 2, we obtain $\tau_X(P)=\bigcap_{\sigma\in G}\tau_X(\sigma_X(A))=\bigcap_{\sigma\in G}(\sigma\circ\tau)_X(A)=P$, since $\sigma\mapsto\sigma\circ\tau$ permutes $G$, with inverse $\rho\mapsto\rho\circ\tau^{-1}$. A bijection also preserves complements, so $\tau_X(Q)=X_L\setminus\tau_X(P)=Q$. This proves every assertion.
